title: Correction of Information on Gov Factually Website
what_it_is: Correction of Information on Gov Factually Website

sections.label: Factually clarifying government policy misperceptions
sections.summary: Factually clarifies common misperceptions of Government policy and inaccurate assertions on public concerns, addressing housing, economy, finance and Zika.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Factually aims to clarify widespread or common misperceptions of Government policy or incorrect assertions on matters of public concern that can harm Singapore's social fabric.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Over the years, the site has addressed inaccurate assertions about various matters, such as housing, the economy and finance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: During the Zika outbreak, we allayed public misperceptions about the virus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Factually, as its name suggests, concerns itself with facts, not opinions.

sections.label: Public engagement sessions raising concerns
sections.summary: Public engagement exercises and sessions are held periodically, and concerns raised by the public are looked into and clarified if misperceptions exist.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, periodically, we do public engagement exercises and sessions, and during these sessions, some concerns may be raised by members of the public and we will look into them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: If we think there is enough of interest in that subject matter that has purveyed some misperceptions, we will clarify.
